1	# ADR-0034: PROJECTOR Scene Shape and Y-Sort
2	
3	## Status
4	Proposed
5	
6	## Date
7	2026-10-29
8	
9	## Last Verified
10	2026-10-29 (against `design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` PR-5 (sort origin, class ranks, z-band table, per-row fallback), C2, C5, C8 and the Y-sort acceptance criteria; `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-31, the engine feasibility note, AC-121, AC-123, AC-140, AC-165, OQ-33; `ship-body-and-interior-physics.md` BDY-26, BDY-27, BDY-33, AC-BDY-69, AC-BDY-92, AC-BDY-92b; `web-map-and-transit.md` WM-14, WM-19, WM-24, E-19; `failure-and-trail-system.md` FT-14 and the dirty-key table; `derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` DA-5, DA-38; `modular-ship-assembly.md` MSA-39; `docs/architecture/architecture.md` § Required ADRs, § Spikes that gate ADRs, OQ-3; `requirements-traceability.md` rows tagged ADR-0034; the Foundation ADRs ADR-0001 to ADR-0010 and the sibling drafts ADR-0011, ADR-0013, ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016 and ADR-0019 (read for their interfaces only); `docs/registry/architecture.yaml` and `design/registry/entities.yaml`; and `docs/engine-reference/godot/` `VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md`, `deprecated-apis.md`, `current-best-practices.md`, `modules/rendering.md`). No code exists. Every engine fact marked "probed 2026-10-29" was run on the installed 4.7.2 mono **editor** binary from `C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/0034/` (outside the repository), with a `SubViewport` read back through `get_texture().get_image()`: probes P1 ran windowed on the default Compatibility (OpenGL 3.3) renderer, P2 on both Forward+ (Vulkan) and Compatibility, P3 to P10 and P13 on Forward+ (Vulkan), P11 and P12 headless. The machine is an RTX 4070 Laptop; nothing was run on a release export, D3D12 or a Steam Deck. Every other engine claim not in the pinned reference is marked UNVERIFIED with the spike or story that settles it.
11	
12	## Decision Makers
13	Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.
14	
15	## Summary
16	The two PROJECTOR subscribers (the Layout projector and `body.projector`) must turn `layout.state`, `body.state` and the frozen section templates into one engine scene in which walls, doors, props, actors and horrors sort by `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`, in which a weld or cut changes which body a section belongs to without a visible frame, and from which the camera solver receives a limits rectangle; the GDDs left the shape to a spike (SP-YSORT-1), which has not run. This ADR decides the shape from probes on the editor binary: one `y_sort_enabled` translation-only root per live body inside one `y_sort_enabled` world node (nested Y-sort nodes sort as one merged group, so a per-body root does not break the single sort scope), seven z-band groups per body root with the sorted ones in a fixed rank order, one `TileMapLayer` per section per layer kind (section offsets sit on a 24 px grid, so a merged per-body 48 px tile map cannot hold them) with exactly one atlas source each, weld and cut by **reparenting** each moved section's nodes and shifting their positions (no tile is rebuilt on a weld), a publisher-namespaced `entity_id` packing in `src/shared/` with registered namespace bytes, and an integer `CameraLimits` rectangle published to the solver in stage `PROJECT`. SP-YSORT-1 stays the acceptance gate for the release export, the Steam Deck, real atlases and the 8 ms weld figure; this ADR is Proposed and does not close it.
17	
18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
23	| **Domain** | Rendering (2D canvas: `CanvasItem` Y-sort, `z_index`, `TileMapLayer`), Core (node tree, reparenting) |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM per `architecture.md` (TileMapLayer and its Y-sort tie rule under reparenting were unverified for 4.7). The pinned reference is silent on `TileMapLayer` and Y-sort: `breaking-changes.md` lists only "`TileMapLayer` replaces `TileMap`" (4.3), "TileMapLayer scene tile rotation" (4.7) and the 4.7 `CanvasItem` line-drawing change; `modules/rendering.md` has no TileMap section; `deprecated-apis.md` lists `TileMap` and `YSort`. Every Y-sort and `TileMapLayer` behaviour below is therefore a probe of the editor binary, not a documented fact, and is marked as such. |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (2D, Rendering, TileMap rows), `deprecated-apis.md` (`TileMap`, `YSort`), `current-best-practices.md` (Rendering 4.7), `modules/rendering.md`. No `tilemap.md` or `2d.md` exists in `modules/`. |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None that are new in 4.4 to 4.7. `TileMapLayer` (4.3), `TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin`, `TileMapLayer.update_internals()`, `Node.reparent(new_parent, keep_global_transform)` (4.0), `CanvasItem.y_sort_enabled` (4.0), `Performance.OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` and `Viewport.get_render_info` exist in 4.7.2 (probed). `TileMap` is not used (deprecated since 4.3). |
27	| **Verification Required** | **Probed 2026-10-29 on the 4.7.2 editor binary, windowed (see Last Verified for the renderer per probe):** (V1) equal Y keys tie by **tree order**, later on top; `move_child` swaps the result; a higher key draws on top regardless of insertion order (P1, P2). (V2) **Nested `y_sort_enabled` nodes sort as one merged group** keyed by the accumulated transform: a y-sorted child group at y 100 holding a sprite at local y -90 (global 10) drew behind a sibling at y 50 (P3); a three-level chain world, body root with a +100 offset, layer merged two bodies by global key (P5, P6, S2, b); a **non-sorting** intermediate node sorts its whole subtree as one unit by its own y (P4), and non-sorting body roots fall back to root tree order (P5b, P5c). (V3) **A `TileMapLayer` with `y_sort_enabled` joins the merged group cell by cell, and its cell key is `cell_top + tile_size.y / 2 + TileData.y_sort_origin + TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin + layer.position.y`**; texture size and `texture_origin` do not enter it; a tile and a sprite at an equal key tie by tree order of the **layer** versus the sprite's layer (P4, P10, P13, a). (V4) `z_index` still orders inside a y-sorted ancestor chain: floor (z 0), y-sorted groups (z 10) and caps (z 20) drew in band order with caps above both (S1). (V5) `Node.reparent(p)` with the default `keep_global_transform = true` **rewrites the local position** (a child at local (10, 10) moved under a parent offset by 100 read local (-90, 10)); `reparent(p, false)` and `remove_child` plus `add_child` keep the local position; all three append the node as the **last child** (P7, S-series). (V6) `Light2D.range_z_min` and `range_z_max` default to -1024 and 1024 and are inclusive at both ends: with a range of 0 to 20 the items at z 30, 900 and 910 were unlit, with 0 to 910 all lit (P9; closes the PR-5 `[UNV]` note). (V7) `Performance.OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` counts parentless live nodes (a detached subtree of 11 read 11; a hidden holder that is **in the tree** reads 0 and its descendants are not visible in the tree) (P11, P12). (V8) Draw calls read with `Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS, RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME)`: 453 cells of one atlas source read 1 call whether or not y-sorted and whether split over one layer or four; **two atlas sources alternating by row read 440 calls unsorted and 23 sorted** (P5, P6); batching follows texture runs in draw order, not node count. (V9) Margin timings on the dev machine, editor binary, Forward+, **evidence only**: `set_cell` x 453 about 0.10 ms; `update_internals()` for 453 y-sorted cells 0.39 ms (13 us unsorted); 256 cells set plus update 0.27 ms; reparenting a 182-cell y-sorted layer 75 us; reparenting 100 sprites 0.26 ms; `move_child` x 100 0.05 ms; freeing a 182-cell layer 0.13 ms. **UNVERIFIED and gated by SP-YSORT-1:** all of V1 to V9 on a release export, on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, with the real atlases and the real 96 px faces; Direct3D 12 is not a target (ADR-0008 pins Vulkan); behaviour of the y-sorted `TileMapLayer` when `rendering_quadrant_size` is set (the project default of 16 is used for unsorted layers only, and the sorted-layer cell cost was probed at the default); any change in these rules in a 4.7 patch release. |
28	
29	## ADR Dependencies
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|-------|-------|
33	| **Depends On** | ADR-0009 (PROJECTOR class rights, stage `PROJECT` and its registration order, `PresenterDescriptor`, `Placement`, chunked rebuild, the single-chunk in-reach rule for Lighting's occluder builder only; Proposed), ADR-0008 (world viewport, body frame as the canvas, `CameraSolver`, z-band names, draw-call table, `RenderLayout`; Proposed), ADR-0013 (sections, bodies, `section_offset`, `welds[]`, sockets, `AttachResult` and `DetachResult`, dirty keys SEC / BODY / SEAM / LEAF, the closed `kind_ordinal` vocabulary; Proposed draft), ADR-0015 (`BodyView` `world` and `world_prev`, `BODY_TRANSFER` records, the canvas-offset formula it hands to this ADR, the 2^22 and 2^24 bounds; Proposed draft), ADR-0004 (dirty keys, `ChangeBatch`, events, merged delivery to `PROJECTOR` subscribers; Proposed), ADR-0003 (read views, `snap_baseline`; Proposed), ADR-0001 (frame order, `PresentationClock`; Proposed), ADR-0010 (the `src/presentation/projector/` and `src/shared/` placement and lint tool; Proposed). **Soft:** ADR-0014 (the rect table the sprites are built from, `section_rects_into`; Proposed draft), ADR-0007 (frozen catalogs, the `LayoutTuning` table, a new `presentation` data domain; Proposed), ADR-0011 (no read required; `GraphView.section_dormant` only for diagnostics; Proposed draft). |
34	| **Enables** | The Layout projector story and the `body.projector` story (both gated, see Ordering Note); ADR-0028 (Lighting: the z range its lights must cover, parenting of its pooled nodes, the occluder builder's place after this ADR's builders); the Failure & Trail, Avatar Presenter, Interaction and Horror presenters (the `attach` API, the namespace table); ADR-0026 (the `ProjectionSet` input it is asked to publish); ADR-0030 (the Pipeline's TRANSIT_HOLD latch reads `ProjectorReadiness`). |
35	| **Blocks** | Epics and stories: Layout PROJECTOR, `body.projector`, Pixel-Perfect Pipeline (limits sink and ready latch), Failure & Trail (draw bands), Avatar Presenter (`attach_presenter`), Modular Ship Assembly (bead, jamb and leaf draw), Web Map & Transit (arrival scene build). |
36	| **Ordering Note** | **Gating, stated honestly.** Spike SP-YSORT-1 (LY-31, AC-165) is the formal gate and has not run. LY-31 asked it to test option B (no reparent, one Y-sort node) first and fall back to option A (per-body roots). The probes in this ADR remove B's premise: B existed to keep "ONE Y-sort `Node2D`", and V2 shows that nested `y_sort_enabled` nodes already form one merged sort scope, so per-body roots do not split it. The spike therefore **confirms** this ADR's shape and measures what the editor probes cannot (release export, RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, real atlases, the 8 ms weld P99 of AC-BDY-69, draw calls with real art); it no longer chooses between B and A. **This ADR stays Proposed. Acceptance requires** SP-YSORT-1 to pass the five LY-31 exit criteria as remapped in § 11 on a release export, ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 Accepted, and the namespace table of § 4 agreed by the owners of the five publishers. **Not blocked on this ADR:** any Foundation coding, any simulation story. The siblings ADR-0013 and ADR-0015 are drafts; the assumptions on them are in `cross_adr_assumptions` of the result and in Open Questions. |
37	
38	## Context
39	
40	### Problem Statement
41	Five things were left to this ADR by the GDDs and by ADR-0008 and ADR-0009, and none can be decided inside a presenter story:
42	
43	1. **Scene shape.** Body's GDD (BDY-33) says a PROJECTOR owns one translation-only root per live body, with one y-sorted actor and props layer per root, and reparents Presenter nodes on `BODY_TRANSFER`. Layout's GDD (LY-31) says the default shape reparents section nodes under that root on every weld, that this "sits badly" with the Pipeline's single Y-sort scope, and that a spike should try a no-reparent option B first. Neither text knows whether nested Y-sort nodes form one scope, whether a weld should reparent or rebuild, or whether a tile map is per body or per section.
44	2. **The Y-sort key.** PR-5 fixes `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` and says the wall-face `y_sort_origin` "is set to the footprint depth, not 0". The engine's own key for a `TileMapLayer` cell is different (V3), the tie rule is tree order (V1), nothing registers the `entity_id` namespaces that make ids unique across blocks (Layout OQ-33), and a door's sort edge depends on a Graph value (TR-pxl-007).
45	3. **Weld, cut and arrival cost.** A weld must show its bead in the first frame (TR-assembly-045), cost at most 8 ms P99 (TR-shipbody-045, a working threshold) and leave no orphan node; an arrival must build the largest destination scene inside the settle window (TR-webmap-037); both are budgeted in `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` units that no ADR has made precise. ADR-0009 OQ-I left the weld case to this ADR.
46	4. **The camera-limits rectangle.** ADR-0009 OQ-C reconciled that a PROJECTOR publishes the rectangle and never writes `Camera2D.limit_*`; no ADR has named the sink, the frame, or the rectangle.
47	5. **Draw bands and the fallback.** The z-band order is "the contract" and the numbers are "the ADR's" (PR-5); the per-row fallback is built only if it wins a measurement (TR-pxl-009).
48	
49	### Constraints
50	- **Presentation never writes the simulation (kernel H4).** The PROJECTOR writes only engine-side derived objects its block owners' GDDs name, never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D` (the Layout projector; ADR-0009 § 1), and never writes `Camera2D.limit_*` (OQ-C).
51	- **Integer placement, one assignment point.** Every `Node2D.position` in presentation is written only through `Placement.put` (ADR-0009 § 4); canvas coordinates are integer-valued `float32` and exact for `|v| <= 2^24` base px (ADR-0008 § 6.2); body-frame and canvas offsets are bounded by ADR-0015 (`WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`).
52	- **Rotation is never rendered inside (C2).** Every body root has rotation 0, scale (1, 1), skew 0.
53	- **`physics_interpolation` is off for all presentation (ADR-0009 § 5); `tick_alpha` is the one interpolator.**
54	- **Stage `PROJECT` (0) runs before `CAMERA_SOLVE` (1) in the same `_process` pass** (ADR-0009 § 3), so anything the projector publishes is consumed in the same frame. The registration order inside stage 0 is the layout projector, then `body.projector`, then Lighting's occluder builder (ADR-0009 § 3).
55	- **Presenters define no `_process` and no handler allocates or draws** (ADR-0009 § 2): the projectors mark dirty in the handler and build in `present`.
56	- **The PROJECTOR scripts live in `src/presentation/projector/`; `src/sim/**` is tree-free** (ADR-0010 § 1.2). Pure packing helpers that the simulation must also compute live in `src/shared/` (L0).
57	- **Section offsets are on the 24 px grid, not the 48 px grid** (ADR-0013 § 7, `GRID_24`; the registry's MVP socket pair gives an offset of 696 px on x, which is 14.5 tiles).
58	- **Walls project up-screen** (PR-5 convention): footprint rows `[y0, y0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`, a face of `WALL_FACE_PX` rising from the footprint's south edge, a cap of `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` above the face.
59	- **Release-export performance is unmeasured (OQ-10); every wall-clock figure here is a proposal or margin evidence.**
60	
61	### Requirements
62	- One tree shape that the weld, cut, pod hop, arrival, restore and salvage paths all produce identically (a test compares an incrementally updated projector with a fresh one fed `ALL`).
63	- A draw order that is a pure function of persisted ids and positions: identical on 10 runs and after a save and reload that reverses creation order (PR-5 acceptance).
64	- A weld frame that moves nodes and shifts positions without building tiles; an arrival that builds in a declared number of frames.
65	- Named bands and a lint that dependents can use without writing a z number.
66	- A limits rectangle in integer base px, in the frame the solver works in, published before the solve.
67	
68	### Binding stances respected (registry check, `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`)
69	No registered stance is contradicted. Stances this ADR builds on: `PresentationStage` constants and the PROJECT order (ADR-0009); `Placement.at` / `put` as the only position writer (ADR-0009 § 4); `camera_canvas_transform_write` (ADR-0008: the solver is the only clamp, `Camera2D.limit_*` untouched, no `Camera2D` in the world tree); canvas exactness to `2^24` (ADR-0008 § 6.2); the layer-first source tree with `src/presentation/projector/` (ADR-0010); ids are block-local and the kernel allocates none (ADR-0003 § 2). One registry-adjacent point is **extended**, not contradicted: the registered constant `LAYOUT_ID_NS` is "to be agreed" in `entities.yaml`; § 4 fixes it. ADR-0003's "entity ids are block-local" rule stands: the `entity_id` of this ADR is a **presentation sort-key composite**, never a block id and never persisted.
70	
71	## Decision
72	
73	### Architecture Diagram
74	
75	```
76	 stage 0 PROJECT (ADR-0009 § 3), one rendered frame, in this registration order
77	 |
78	 |-(1) Layout projector (PROJECTOR facet; subscribes layout.state only; reads door_passage and the rect table)
79	 |       dirty keys SEC / BODY / SEAM / LEAF / ALL  ->  per-section SectionScene objects (RefCounted handles)
80	 |       builds in the hidden Staging holder, <= BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME work units a frame, commits atomically
81	 |       never parents under a body root: it hands finished SectionScenes to body.projector
82	 |
83	 |-(2) body.projector (PROJECTOR facet; subscribes body.state, layout.state, web.state)
84	 |       BodyRoot per body in the ProjectionSet; mounts / moves SectionScenes; reparents + shifts on weld and cut;
85	 |       attach / attach_presenter / detach; writes root canvas offsets; WM-19 visibility;
86	 |       publishes CameraLimits (integer rect) and ProjectorReadiness
87	 |
88	 |-(3) Lighting occluder builder (ADR-0028)  -- unchanged by this ADR; reads the rect table, not these nodes
89	 v
90	 stage 1 CAMERA_SOLVE reads CameraLimits in the same frame
91	 stage 2.. AVATAR / TRAIL / ... write positions of nodes they attached (Placement.put)
92	
93	 scene tree under the WorldViewport (ADR-0008 § 2)       y = y_sort_enabled, z = z_index (absolute here: parents are z 0)
94	 ProjectorRoot : Node2D                                  not sorted, z 0
95	 +- Staging : Node2D                                     visible = false, IN the tree (no orphan noise), never drawn
96	 +- World : Node2D                                       y = TRUE   (the one sort scope's top)
97	    +- BodyRoot[body_id ascending] : Node2D              y = TRUE, translation only, rotation 0, scale (1,1), skew 0
98	         position = canvas_offset_render(body); visible = InteriorDrawRule (WM-19)
99	         |- Floor        : Node2D  z = ZBand.FLOOR  (0)    y = false   per-section floor TileMapLayer (position = section_offset)
100	         |- Marks        : Node2D  z = ZBand.MARKS  (1)    y = false   foreign: floor trails, stains (Failure & Trail)
101	         |- Faces        : Node2D  z = ZBand.YSORT (10)    y = TRUE    class_rank 0: per-section wall-face TileMapLayer
102	         |- Mounted      : Node2D  z = ZBand.YSORT (10)    y = TRUE    class_rank 1: per-section mounted TileMapLayer, then sorted sprites
103	         |- PropsActors  : Node2D  z = ZBand.YSORT (10)    y = TRUE    class_rank 2 then 3, children in (class_rank, entity_id) order
104	         |- Caps         : Node2D  z = ZBand.CAPS  (20)    y = false   per-section cap TileMapLayer
105	         '- Dust         : Node2D  z = ZBand.DUST  (30)    y = false   foreign: dust, mist, venting (never Y-sorted)
106	
107	 merged sort scope = every node on a chain of y_sort_enabled ancestors from World down to a sorted group (V2);
108	 cross-body equal keys fall to BodyRoot order (body_id ascending); within a body the group order Faces < Mounted < PropsActors
109	 is the class-rank order, and inside PropsActors child order is (class_rank, entity_id).
110	```
111	
112	### 1. The decisions at a glance
113	
114	| Point (from the scope) | Decision | Where |
115	|---|---|---|
116	| Per-body roots | **Yes.** One `y_sort_enabled`, translation-only `BodyRoot` per body in the `ProjectionSet`, under one `y_sort_enabled` `World`. The root, not each node, carries the canvas offset. | § 2 |
117	| Reparent versus rebuild | **Reparent and shift** every moved section's nodes on weld and cut; **no tile is rebuilt**. Rebuild (chunked, staged, atomic) happens only on first build, arrival, restore, `ALL`, and a section whose template or discard state changed. A fresh-build path stays the reference: a signature test requires both paths to give equal scenes. | § 7 |
118	| Per-body versus per-section `TileMapLayer` | **Per section**, one layer per layer kind (floor, wall face, mounted, cap), **exactly one `TileSetAtlasSource` each**. | § 5 |
119	| Y-sort key | `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` realised as: engine key = integer node position (sprites) or `cell_top + tile_h/2 + origins` (tiles); class rank = group order; `entity_id` = child order of the sorted layers. Door and wall sort edges as in § 3. | § 3 |
120	| `entity_id` namespaces | `EntityId.pack(ns, local)` in `src/shared/`; namespace bytes **LAYOUT 1, BODY 2, INTERACTION 3, HORROR 4, SUIT 5, WEB 6, TRAIL 7**, 8 to 127 reserved append-only; Layout's local part as LY-31. | § 4 |
121	| Camera-limit rectangle | Integer base-px rect of the avatar's body: union of `[offset, offset + size_tiles x TILE_PX)` over its sections, grown north by `WALL_FACE_PX + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`, published as `CameraLimits` in stage `PROJECT`; the solver is the only clamp. | § 9 |
122	| SP-YSORT-1 | Confirms; does not choose. | § 11 |
123	
124	### 2. The scene tree
125	
126	The tree in the diagram is the contract. Rules, each lint- or boot-checked (§ Validation):
127	
128	- **`World` and every `BodyRoot` have `y_sort_enabled = true`.** That is what makes the sort scope one merged group across bodies (V2). A `BodyRoot` is never made non-sorting: a non-sorting intermediate sorts its whole subtree as a unit (V2, P4), which would turn cross-body ordering into root order.
129	- **`BodyRoot` is translation only**: `rotation == 0`, `scale == (1, 1)`, `skew == 0` every frame (TR-pxl-018, C2 consequence (i)); only `Placement.put` writes `position`. A detached section keeps rotation 0 and simply gets its own root (TR-pxl-018 "detached sections translate without rotation").
130	- **Seven groups per root, in the order drawn above, created with the root and freed with it.** `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors` are the only sorting groups. `Floor`, `Marks`, `Caps` and `Dust` have `y_sort_enabled = false`; their z band keeps them out of the sort (V4). The PR-5 lint "the cap `TileMapLayer` is not a child of the Y-sort node" is therefore restated by band, not by ancestry (GDD sync).
131	- **`z_index` is set once, on the group, from `ZBand` names; `z_as_relative` stays at its default `true` and every ancestor of a group has z 0**, so the group's z is its absolute z. No other node writes `z_index`, and no presenter writes a z number (lint `PJT-03`).
132	- **The `World` node is the only Y-sort scope for the interior.** Exterior and transit layers (parallax, silhouettes, the pod in transit) are the camera host's and the Web Map presenter's and are not under `World`; the projector creates no exterior layer (TR-pxl-018, owned by ADR-0008).
133	
134	**The z bands (names are the contract, TR-pxl-008).**
135	
136	| Name | z | Sorted | Group | Contents |
137	|---|---|---|---|---|
138	| `ZBand.FLOOR` | 0 | never | `Floor` | floor `TileMapLayer`s; grates and drains |
139	| `ZBand.MARKS` | +1 | never | `Marks` | floor trails, stains, footprints (foreign, Trail); drawn flat, authoring order |
140	| `ZBand.YSORT` | +10 | yes | `Faces`, `Mounted`, `PropsActors` | wall faces; wall-mounted items and wall trails; doors, props, machinery, actors, horrors, deployables, empty suits, off-floor web pieces |
141	| `ZBand.CAPS` | +20 | never | `Caps` | cap `TileMapLayer`s; free-hanging housings |
142	| `ZBand.DUST` | +30 | never | `Dust` | `GPUParticles2D` (foreign) |
143	
144	Floor marks and wall trails keep the PR-5 assignment: floor trails at `MARKS` and never sorted; wall trails in `Mounted` at their host face's sort origin (TR-ftrail-017); "no trail uses z 0 or +20" holds because a trail node can only be attached to `MARKS`, `Mounted` or `Dust` and the projector, not the trail, sets z. All five values sit inside the default `Light2D` range of -1024 to 1024, which is inclusive and was probed (V6); Lighting (ADR-0028) must set every light's `range_z_min <= ZBand.FLOOR` and `range_z_max >= ZBand.DUST`, and the fallback table of § 10 raises the largest value to 910, still inside. The numeric values live in one file, `src/presentation/projector/z_band.gd`, and dependents lint names, never numbers.
145	
146	**Caps-above safety (TR-pxl-008).** Caps draw above the sorted band, which is correct iff no item flush against a wall has a face taller than `WALL_FACE_PX`. This is a kit rule; the debug tree-walk keeps the GDD's `diag.cap_overlap` (a prop whose drawn height exceeds the face) and `diag.actor_in_footprint` (a foot row inside a wall footprint) as dev and test checks in `ProjectorAudit`.
147	
148	### 3. The Y-sort key, as built
149	
150	The contract key is `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` with class ranks 0 wall-face tiles, 1 wall-mounted items, 2 doors, props, machinery, deployables, empty suits and off-floor web pieces, 3 actors and horrors. Godot gives us the first term and the tree order; the other two are realised by structure:
151	
152	| Term | Realised by |
153	|---|---|
154	| `sort_y` | The engine key: a node's accumulated y for a `Node2D`; for a `TileMapLayer` cell, `cell_top + tile_size.y / 2 + TileData.y_sort_origin + TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin + layer.position.y` (V3). All terms are integers. |
155	| `class_rank` | The order of the sorted groups under a body root (`Faces` before `Mounted` before `PropsActors`) plus, inside `PropsActors`, rank 2 children before rank 3 children. An equal key ties by tree order (V1), so the earlier group draws first. |
156	| `entity_id` | The child order of a sorted layer. Children are kept in ascending `(class_rank, entity_id)` by `SortedLayer` (§ 3.3), so an equal key and rank resolve by `entity_id` ascending, never by `x` and never by creation order. |
157	
158	**3.1 Sort origins (integer base px, TR-pxl-006).**
159	- **Actors and horrors**: the foot row. The Presenter writes the node `position` to the integer `(p.x, p.y)` (BDY-33 (e)), so the key is `y_foot`, already floored by `Placement.at`; an actor at 239.6 sorts as 239.
160	- **Walls, doors, props, machinery nodes**: the south edge of the footprint.
161	- **Anything mounted on a wall face** (pipes, fittings, seams, gauges, the emissive overlay, wall trails, bead, plate, scar): its host face's sort origin, drawn after the face by group order.
162	- **Doors and doorways (TR-pxl-007).** `sort_y = y_0` (the footprint's north edge) when the doorway is open, and `sort_y = y_0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` when it is closed (a closed door sorts as a wall). The projector computes it in `DoorSort.sort_y(y0, open_extent_px)` (a pure function) from Layout's `door_passage_into(section_id, via_id, out)` record (`open_extent_px`, ADR-0013 § 8 and § 11), and writes the leaf sprite's position through `Placement.put` when it re-reads the leaf on a `LEAF/<section_id>` key (ADR-0013 § 8 marks LEAF whenever a leaf rect changes, and `area` leaving zero changes the leaf rect). Reading the Layout record, not the Graph, means the Layout projector subscribes to `layout.state` alone (the Graph dirties keys every step and would wake stage 0 needlessly) and needs no edge-id reverse lookup; for a mated hatch the record is read once per section, so both leaves agree. **Equivalence with `area > 0`:** D.5 defines `open_extent_px = gap(area)`, which is 0 when closed and positive for every `area >= 1` provided the authored `area_max` does not exceed the doorway width in px; a larger `area_max` would draw a barely-open leaf at its closed edge, so an `area_max <= doorway width` invariant is asked of ADR-0013 (OQ-E). The leaf sprite's drawn extent equals the leaf rect with no tween (TR-section-013).
163	
164	**3.2 The tile convention (a GDD-sync item, PR-5).** The engine measures `y_sort_origin` from the **cell centre**, not the cell top (V3). The GDD text "set to the footprint depth, not 0" is therefore right only for one cell convention. This ADR pins it: **wall-face and wall-mounted `TileMapLayer`s use a cell height of `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`** (one 24-row GRID_24 row; the cell width is the art bible's cell rule and does not enter the key), `TileData.y_sort_origin = 0` on every tile, and the **layer's** `y_sort_origin = WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH / 2` (one value per layer; boot invariant `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` is even). A wall whose footprint is rows `[y0, y0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)` sits in cell row `y0 / WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (GRID_24), so its key is `y0 + depth / 2 + depth / 2 = y0 + depth`, the south edge, and the PR-5 acceptance example (footprint rows 240 to 264, key 264) holds. The 72 px face and 24 px cap art is taller than the cell and hangs up-screen through the tile's `texture_origin`, which does not enter the key (V3). The floor and cap layers are never sorted, so they need no origin.
165	
166	**3.3 `SortedLayer`: how `(class_rank, entity_id)` order is kept.**
167	
168	```gdscript
169	# src/presentation/projector/sorted_layer.gd
170	class_name SortedLayer extends RefCounted
171	## Wraps one sorted group node. Children are kept in ascending (class_rank, entity_id); the parallel arrays hold the order.
172	var _nodes: Array[Node2D]
173	var _rank: PackedByteArray
174	var _eid: PackedInt64Array
175	func insert(node: Node2D, class_rank: int, entity_id: int) -> int   ## OK or ERR_DUPLICATE_ID; binary search, add_child, move_child to the index
176	func remove(node: Node2D) -> bool                                     ## removes from the parallel arrays; does not free
177	func merge_from(other: SortedLayer) -> void                           ## one pass: both inputs are sorted, so compute final indices, then move_child once per node
178	func count() -> int
179	```
180	`insert` finds the index by binary search over `(rank, eid)`, calls `add_child` and then `move_child(node, index)`; a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)` is refused (counted as `diag.sort_id_collision`, which must stay zero) rather than silently ordered by tree position. `merge_from` serves the weld: the survivor's and the absorbed body's `PropsActors` are each already sorted, so the merged order is one linear pass followed by one `move_child` per node (V9: 100 moves cost 0.05 ms on the dev machine). **Tiles carry no `entity_id`**: wall-face and wall-mounted tiles are rank 0 and 1 and tie among themselves by cell position, which is the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`; the sprites of rank 1 are children of `Mounted` after its tile layers.
181	
182	**3.4 Cross-body equal keys (a stated exception).** Within a body the order is exactly the contract. Across two bodies whose interiors are both drawn (docked, WM-19) an equal key with overlapping sprites falls to `BodyRoot` order, ascending `body_id`, which the projector maintains with `move_child`. For Layout pieces that coincides with ascending `entity_id` whenever section ids and body ids were allocated in the same order, which holds for the MVP builds (`init_world` builds home first); it is not guaranteed after cuts. The region where this can occur is the mating seam of two docked hulls. It is tested as a bounded exception (AC-123 (b) is run within one body; the cross-body case is a recorded SP-YSORT-1 observation, § 11) and listed in Risks.
183	
184	### 4. `entity_id` and its namespaces
185	
186	`entity_id` is **a presentation sort-key composite**, not a block id. It is a pure function of persisted ids, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one and is never stored. ADR-0003's rule (ids are block-local, cross-block references are `(block_id, entity_id)`) is unchanged.
187	
188	```gdscript
189	# src/shared/entity_id.gd (L0: pure ints, no engine types; sim modules and presentation both may call it)
190	class_name EntityId extends RefCounted
191	const NS_SHIFT: int = 56
192	const LOCAL_MASK: int = (1 << 56) - 1
193	static func pack(ns: int, local: int) -> int           ## (ns << 56) | local; ns in 1..127; local in 0..LOCAL_MASK; asserts in debug, returns 0 (invalid) otherwise
194	static func ns_of(id: int) -> int
195	static func local_of(id: int) -> int
196	static func layout_local(section_id: int, kind_ordinal: int, idx: int) -> int   ## (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | idx
197	# src/shared/entity_ns.gd : the namespace table (append-only; a golden test pins it)
198	class_name EntityNs extends RefCounted
199	const LAYOUT: int = 1       # door leaf, jamb, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar sprites
200	const BODY: int = 2         # actors (local = actor_id)
201	const INTERACTION: int = 3  # loose items, deployables (local = item_id)
202	const HORROR: int = 4       # horror rigs (local = horror entity_id)
203	const SUIT: int = 5         # empty suits and carried-and-dropped suit props
204	const WEB: int = 6          # off-floor web pieces
205	const TRAIL: int = 7        # trail sprites (local = the Graph subject key)
206	# 8..127: reserved, append-only
207	```
208	- **The sign.** A namespace byte of 1 to 127 keeps every id positive in GDScript's signed 64-bit `int`, so ids compare as plain integers (the Pipeline never needs an unsigned compare). `0` is invalid.
209	- **Layout's local part** is LY-31's: `section_id` below `2^20` (ADR-0013 § 3 guarantees it), `kind_ordinal` in 8 bits, `idx` in 16 bits (the rect `idx` or the template placement index, below the rect stride, ADR-0013 § 13). `kind_ordinal` values are assigned append-only: `DOOR_LEAF 1`, `PROP 2`, `MACHINE 3`, `BEAD 4`, `PLATE 5`, `SCAR 6`, and **`JAMB 7`**, which TR-assembly-045 requires and ADR-0013 § 13's closed list of six does not name (an assumption on ADR-0013, in `cross_adr_assumptions`). Class ranks: `BEAD`, `PLATE`, `SCAR` are rank 1 (the wall-mounted layer, LY-33); `DOOR_LEAF`, `JAMB`, `PROP`, `MACHINE` are rank 2.
210	- **Other publishers' local parts** are their own persisted ids: Body's `actor_id` (an `int64` counter, asserted below `2^56`), Interaction's `item_id`, Horror's `entity_id`. Each publisher calls `EntityId.pack` itself; Layout exports no helper (ADR-0013 § 13), so the Layout projector packs, using only persisted ids.
211	- **Ordering consequence.** At an equal key and rank, namespaces order ascending: a Layout prop draws before an Interaction item, a Body actor before a horror. That is deterministic and save-stable; it is a convention, not a design claim.
212	- **Guard.** `SortedLayer.insert` refuses a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)`; a golden test pins the namespace table; a lint forbids `EntityId.pack` with a literal namespace outside `entity_ns.gd` (`PJT-08`).
213	
214	### 5. Section scenes: per-section layers, one atlas each
215

13	Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.

15	## Summary
16	The two PROJECTOR subscribers (the Layout projector and `body.projector`) must turn `layout.state`, `body.state` and the frozen section templates into one engine scene in which walls, doors, props, actors and horrors sort by `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`, in which a weld or cut changes which body a section belongs to without a visible frame, and from which the camera solver receives a limits rectangle; the GDDs left the shape to a spike (SP-YSORT-1), which has not run. This ADR decides the shape from probes on the editor binary: one `y_sort_enabled` translation-only root per live body inside one `y_sort_enabled` world node (nested Y-sort nodes sort as one merged group, so a per-body root does not break the single sort scope), seven z-band groups per body root with the sorted ones in a fixed rank order, one `TileMapLayer` per section per layer kind (section offsets sit on a 24 px grid, so a merged per-body 48 px tile map cannot hold them) with exactly one atlas source each, weld and cut by **reparenting** each moved section's nodes and shifting their positions (no tile is rebuilt on a weld), a publisher-namespaced `entity_id` packing in `src/shared/` with registered namespace bytes, and an integer `CameraLimits` rectangle published to the solver in stage `PROJECT`. SP-YSORT-1 stays the acceptance gate for the release export, the Steam Deck, real atlases and the 8 ms weld figure; this ADR is Proposed and does not close it.
17	
18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
23	| **Domain** | Rendering (2D canvas: `CanvasItem` Y-sort, `z_index`, `TileMapLayer`), Core (node tree, reparenting) |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM per `architecture.md` (TileMapLayer and its Y-sort tie rule under reparenting were unverified for 4.7). The pinned reference is silent on `TileMapLayer` and Y-sort: `breaking-changes.md` lists only "`TileMapLayer` replaces `TileMap`" (4.3), "TileMapLayer scene tile rotation" (4.7) and the 4.7 `CanvasItem` line-drawing change; `modules/rendering.md` has no TileMap section; `deprecated-apis.md` lists `TileMap` and `YSort`. Every Y-sort and `TileMapLayer` behaviour below is therefore a probe of the editor binary, not a documented fact, and is marked as such. |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (2D, Rendering, TileMap rows), `deprecated-apis.md` (`TileMap`, `YSort`), `current-best-practices.md` (Rendering 4.7), `modules/rendering.md`. No `tilemap.md` or `2d.md` exists in `modules/`. |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None that are new in 4.4 to 4.7. `TileMapLayer` (4.3), `TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin`, `TileMapLayer.update_internals()`, `Node.reparent(new_parent, keep_global_transform)` (4.0), `CanvasItem.y_sort_enabled` (4.0), `Performance.OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` and `Viewport.get_render_info` exist in 4.7.2 (probed). `TileMap` is not used (deprecated since 4.3). |

124	### 2. The scene tree
125	
126	The tree in the diagram is the contract. Rules, each lint- or boot-checked (§ Validation):
127	
128	- **`World` and every `BodyRoot` have `y_sort_enabled = true`.** That is what makes the sort scope one merged group across bodies (V2). A `BodyRoot` is never made non-sorting: a non-sorting intermediate sorts its whole subtree as a unit (V2, P4), which would turn cross-body ordering into root order.
129	- **`BodyRoot` is translation only**: `rotation == 0`, `scale == (1, 1)`, `skew == 0` every frame (TR-pxl-018, C2 consequence (i)); only `Placement.put` writes `position`. A detached section keeps rotation 0 and simply gets its own root (TR-pxl-018 "detached sections translate without rotation").
130	- **Seven groups per root, in the order drawn above, created with the root and freed with it.** `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors` are the only sorting groups. `Floor`, `Marks`, `Caps` and `Dust` have `y_sort_enabled = false`; their z band keeps them out of the sort (V4). The PR-5 lint "the cap `TileMapLayer` is not a child of the Y-sort node" is therefore restated by band, not by ancestry (GDD sync).
131	- **`z_index` is set once, on the group, from `ZBand` names; `z_as_relative` stays at its default `true` and every ancestor of a group has z 0**, so the group's z is its absolute z. No other node writes `z_index`, and no presenter writes a z number (lint `PJT-03`).
132	- **The `World` node is the only Y-sort scope for the interior.** Exterior and transit layers (parallax, silhouettes, the pod in transit) are the camera host's and the Web Map presenter's and are not under `World`; the projector creates no exterior layer (TR-pxl-018, owned by ADR-0008).

148	### 3. The Y-sort key, as built
149	
150	The contract key is `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` with class ranks 0 wall-face tiles, 1 wall-mounted items, 2 doors, props, machinery, deployables, empty suits and off-floor web pieces, 3 actors and horrors. Godot gives us the first term and the tree order; the other two are realised by structure:
151	
152	| Term | Realised by |
153	|---|---|
154	| `sort_y` | The engine key: a node's accumulated y for a `Node2D`; for a `TileMapLayer` cell, `cell_top + tile_size.y / 2 + TileData.y_sort_origin + TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin + layer.position.y` (V3). All terms are integers. |
155	| `class_rank` | The order of the sorted groups under a body root (`Faces` before `Mounted` before `PropsActors`) plus, inside `PropsActors`, rank 2 children before rank 3 children. An equal key ties by tree order (V1), so the earlier group draws first. |
156	| `entity_id` | The child order of a sorted layer. Children are kept in ascending `(class_rank, entity_id)` by `SortedLayer` (§ 3.3), so an equal key and rank resolve by `entity_id` ascending, never by `x` and never by creation order. |
157	
158	**3.1 Sort origins (integer base px, TR-pxl-006).**
159	- **Actors and horrors**: the foot row. The Presenter writes the node `position` to the integer `(p.x, p.y)` (BDY-33 (e)), so the key is `y_foot`, already floored by `Placement.at`; an actor at 239.6 sorts as 239.
160	- **Walls, doors, props, machinery nodes**: the south edge of the footprint.
161	- **Anything mounted on a wall face** (pipes, fittings, seams, gauges, the emissive overlay, wall trails, bead, plate, scar): its host face's sort origin, drawn after the face by group order.
162	- **Doors and doorways (TR-pxl-007).** `sort_y = y_0` (the footprint's north edge) when the doorway is open, and `sort_y = y_0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` when it is closed (a closed door sorts as a wall). The projector computes it in `DoorSort.sort_y(y0, open_extent_px)` (a pure function) from Layout's `door_passage_into(section_id, via_id, out)` record (`open_extent_px`, ADR-0013 § 8 and § 11), and writes the leaf sprite's position through `Placement.put` when it re-reads the leaf on a `LEAF/<section_id>` key (ADR-0013 § 8 marks LEAF whenever a leaf rect changes, and `area` leaving zero changes the leaf rect). Reading the Layout record, not the Graph, means the Layout projector subscribes to `layout.state` alone (the Graph dirties keys every step and would wake stage 0 needlessly) and needs no edge-id reverse lookup; for a mated hatch the record is read once per section, so both leaves agree. **Equivalence with `area > 0`:** D.5 defines `open_extent_px = gap(area)`, which is 0 when closed and positive for every `area >= 1` provided the authored `area_max` does not exceed the doorway width in px; a larger `area_max` would draw a barely-open leaf at its closed edge, so an `area_max <= doorway width` invariant is asked of ADR-0013 (OQ-E). The leaf sprite's drawn extent equals the leaf rect with no tween (TR-section-013).
163	
164	**3.2 The tile convention (a GDD-sync item, PR-5).** The engine measures `y_sort_origin` from the **cell centre**, not the cell top (V3). The GDD text "set to the footprint depth, not 0" is therefore right only for one cell convention. This ADR pins it: **wall-face and wall-mounted `TileMapLayer`s use a cell height of `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`** (one 24-row GRID_24 row; the cell width is the art bible's cell rule and does not enter the key), `TileData.y_sort_origin = 0` on every tile, and the **layer's** `y_sort_origin = WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH / 2` (one value per layer; boot invariant `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` is even). A wall whose footprint is rows `[y0, y0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)` sits in cell row `y0 / WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (GRID_24), so its key is `y0 + depth / 2 + depth / 2 = y0 + depth`, the south edge, and the PR-5 acceptance example (footprint rows 240 to 264, key 264) holds. The 72 px face and 24 px cap art is taller than the cell and hangs up-screen through the tile's `texture_origin`, which does not enter the key (V3). The floor and cap layers are never sorted, so they need no origin.
165	
166	**3.3 `SortedLayer`: how `(class_rank, entity_id)` order is kept.**
167	
168	```gdscript
169	# src/presentation/projector/sorted_layer.gd
170	class_name SortedLayer extends RefCounted
171	## Wraps one sorted group node. Children are kept in ascending (class_rank, entity_id); the parallel arrays hold the order.
172	var _nodes: Array[Node2D]
173	var _rank: PackedByteArray
174	var _eid: PackedInt64Array
175	func insert(node: Node2D, class_rank: int, entity_id: int) -> int   ## OK or ERR_DUPLICATE_ID; binary search, add_child, move_child to the index
176	func remove(node: Node2D) -> bool                                     ## removes from the parallel arrays; does not free
177	func merge_from(other: SortedLayer) -> void                           ## one pass: both inputs are sorted, so compute final indices, then move_child once per node
178	func count() -> int
179	```
180	`insert` finds the index by binary search over `(rank, eid)`, calls `add_child` and then `move_child(node, index)`; a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)` is refused (counted as `diag.sort_id_collision`, which must stay zero) rather than silently ordered by tree position. `merge_from` serves the weld: the survivor's and the absorbed body's `PropsActors` are each already sorted, so the merged order is one linear pass followed by one `move_child` per node (V9: 100 moves cost 0.05 ms on the dev machine). **Tiles carry no `entity_id`**: wall-face and wall-mounted tiles are rank 0 and 1 and tie among themselves by cell position, which is the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`; the sprites of rank 1 are children of `Mounted` after its tile layers.
181	
182	**3.4 Cross-body equal keys (a stated exception).** Within a body the order is exactly the contract. Across two bodies whose interiors are both drawn (docked, WM-19) an equal key with overlapping sprites falls to `BodyRoot` order, ascending `body_id`, which the projector maintains with `move_child`. For Layout pieces that coincides with ascending `entity_id` whenever section ids and body ids were allocated in the same order, which holds for the MVP builds (`init_world` builds home first); it is not guaranteed after cuts. The region where this can occur is the mating seam of two docked hulls. It is tested as a bounded exception (AC-123 (b) is run within one body; the cross-body case is a recorded SP-YSORT-1 observation, § 11) and listed in Risks.
183	
184	### 4. `entity_id` and its namespaces
185	
186	`entity_id` is **a presentation sort-key composite**, not a block id. It is a pure function of persisted ids, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one and is never stored. ADR-0003's rule (ids are block-local, cross-block references are `(block_id, entity_id)`) is unchanged.
187	
188	```gdscript
189	# src/shared/entity_id.gd (L0: pure ints, no engine types; sim modules and presentation both may call it)
190	class_name EntityId extends RefCounted
191	const NS_SHIFT: int = 56
192	const LOCAL_MASK: int = (1 << 56) - 1
193	static func pack(ns: int, local: int) -> int           ## (ns << 56) | local; ns in 1..127; local in 0..LOCAL_MASK; asserts in debug, returns 0 (invalid) otherwise
194	static func ns_of(id: int) -> int
195	static func local_of(id: int) -> int
196	static func layout_local(section_id: int, kind_ordinal: int, idx: int) -> int   ## (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | idx
197	# src/shared/entity_ns.gd : the namespace table (append-only; a golden test pins it)
198	class_name EntityNs extends RefCounted
199	const LAYOUT: int = 1       # door leaf, jamb, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar sprites
200	const BODY: int = 2         # actors (local = actor_id)
201	const INTERACTION: int = 3  # loose items, deployables (local = item_id)
202	const HORROR: int = 4       # horror rigs (local = horror entity_id)
203	const SUIT: int = 5         # empty suits and carried-and-dropped suit props
204	const WEB: int = 6          # off-floor web pieces
205	const TRAIL: int = 7        # trail sprites (local = the Graph subject key)
206	# 8..127: reserved, append-only
207	```
208	- **The sign.** A namespace byte of 1 to 127 keeps every id positive in GDScript's signed 64-bit `int`, so ids compare as plain integers (the Pipeline never needs an unsigned compare). `0` is invalid.
209	- **Layout's local part** is LY-31's: `section_id` below `2^20` (ADR-0013 § 3 guarantees it), `kind_ordinal` in 8 bits, `idx` in 16 bits (the rect `idx` or the template placement index, below the rect stride, ADR-0013 § 13). `kind_ordinal` values are assigned append-only: `DOOR_LEAF 1`, `PROP 2`, `MACHINE 3`, `BEAD 4`, `PLATE 5`, `SCAR 6`, and **`JAMB 7`**, which TR-assembly-045 requires and ADR-0013 § 13's closed list of six does not name (an assumption on ADR-0013, in `cross_adr_assumptions`). Class ranks: `BEAD`, `PLATE`, `SCAR` are rank 1 (the wall-mounted layer, LY-33); `DOOR_LEAF`, `JAMB`, `PROP`, `MACHINE` are rank 2.
210	- **Other publishers' local parts** are their own persisted ids: Body's `actor_id` (an `int64` counter, asserted below `2^56`), Interaction's `item_id`, Horror's `entity_id`. Each publisher calls `EntityId.pack` itself; Layout exports no helper (ADR-0013 § 13), so the Layout projector packs, using only persisted ids.
211	- **Ordering consequence.** At an equal key and rank, namespaces order ascending: a Layout prop draws before an Interaction item, a Body actor before a horror. That is deterministic and save-stable; it is a convention, not a design claim.
212	- **Guard.** `SortedLayer.insert` refuses a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)`; a golden test pins the namespace table; a lint forbids `EntityId.pack` with a literal namespace outside `entity_ns.gd` (`PJT-08`).
213	
214	### 5. Section scenes: per-section layers, one atlas each
215

214	### 5. Section scenes: per-section layers, one atlas each
215	
216	**Per-section `TileMapLayer`, decided by arithmetic.** Section offsets lie on the 24 px grid and welded sections are placed by `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b` (ADR-0013 § 7). The registry's MVP pair gives a 696 px offset, which is 14.5 floor tiles, so the cells of two welded sections do not share one 48 px cell grid and **no single per-body tile map can hold both**. Each section therefore owns its own layers, positioned at its integer `section_offset`. Other reasons point the same way and are secondary: a `SEC` change, a discard (LM4) or a dormancy change rebuilds or frees one section only; the maintained and `_worn` atlases (DA-5) differ per section, so a merged layer would mix two atlas sources, and V8 shows that is the expensive case.
217	
218	**The layers per section** (up to four `TileMapLayer`s, each `tile_set` shared across sections of the same atlas set and layer kind through a `TileSetCache` keyed `(atlas_set, layer_kind)`):
219	
220	| Layer kind | Group | Sorted | Cell | `y_sort_origin` |
221	|---|---|---|---|---|
222	| floor | `Floor` | no | `TILE_PX` square, `rendering_quadrant_size` 16 (ADR-0008 § 7.1) | n/a |
223	| wall face | `Faces` | yes (`y_sort_enabled`) | height `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` | `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH / 2` on the layer |
224	| wall mounted | `Mounted` | yes | height `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` | same |
225	| cap | `Caps` | no | 48 x 24 slices (PR-5 z-band table) | n/a |
226	
227	**One atlas source per layer (mandatory).** Each `TileSet` used by a layer holds exactly one `TileSetAtlasSource`. V8 is the reason: the same 453 cells read 1 draw call from one source and 440 from two sources that alternate by row. Sprites use `AtlasTexture` regions of the same sheet so they batch with it; a `_worn` section uses the `_worn` sheet, so a draw-call boundary appears at the section boundary only. This is a production rule for the asset spec (art bible 8.4 to 8.6) and a boot check in the `TileSetCache`.
228	
229	**Atlas selection by template (TR-derelict-028, DA-5).** A presentation table `assets/data/presentation/atlas_map.json` (a new data domain for ADR-0007; integer-only, closed schema, manifest-listed) maps `template_id` to `atlas_set` in `{MAINTAINED, WORN}`. The projector selects the sheet by `template_id` read from `layout.state` and the map; **no Layout field carries wear** and the kit manifest rows name no template, so procgen can reuse them. Boot lints: `ATLAS_MAP_TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN` and `ATLAS_MAP_MISSING` (every catalog template has exactly one row). The table is not persisted and has no ledger.
230	
231	**Sprites** (door leaves, jambs, props, machinery nodes, bead, plate, scar pieces) are built from the rect table (`section_rects_into`, ADR-0014: rows carry `idx`, flags and the current extent) and the template's visual rows (kit-piece ids and layers, the `visual_hash` part of the frozen template, ADR-0013 § 4), not from tiles. Each carries `entity_id = EntityId.pack(EntityNs.LAYOUT, layout_local(section_id, kind_ordinal, idx))` and its class rank from § 4. Socket-state sprites (PLATE, JAMB, LEAF, bead, scar) are rebuilt from `welds[]` and the socket rows on `SEC`, `SEAM` and `LEAF` keys.
232	
233	**Two projectors, one handoff.** The Layout projector builds and owns a `SectionScene` per live section; `body.projector` owns bodies and roots and mounts scenes. ADR-0009 registers the layout projector first, then `body.projector`, which would force a body root to exist before the Layout projector can parent into it; that is avoided by having the Layout projector build **into the hidden `Staging` holder** and never into a body root. A `SectionScene` exposes `mount(body_root_set, section_offset)` and `unmount()` that only `body.projector` calls; when the Layout projector later swaps a rebuilt layer it asks the scene to `swap_in`, and the scene replaces its node under whatever parent it is currently mounted on. The registration order of ADR-0009 is therefore unchanged and sufficient.
234	
235	```gdscript
236	# src/presentation/projector/section_scene.gd
237	class_name SectionScene extends RefCounted
238	var section_id: int
239	var template_id: String
240	var mounted_body_id: int          # 0 while only staged
241	var mounted_off_x: int
242	var mounted_off_y: int
243	var floor_layer: TileMapLayer
244	var face_layer: TileMapLayer
245	var mounted_layer: TileMapLayer
246	var cap_layer: TileMapLayer
247	var layout_sprites: Array[Node2D] # Layout-namespace sprites in (class_rank, entity_id) order
248	var built_static_version: int
249	var complete: bool                # all work units done and committed
250	```
251	
252	### 6. Building: work units, staging, atomic commit, readiness
253	
254	**Work unit.** One `TileMapLayer.set_cell` call or one sprite node created and configured is one **work unit**. The knob `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` (a Layout GDD tuning knob, read from the frozen `LayoutTuning` table, ADR-0007 § 1.5; the module source carries no literal) is the units per `present` call. The unit is named after tiles because tiles dominate (the GDD's tile counts for the MVP world and for the largest destination scene are its sizing basis); sprites are counted in it so that "builds N tiles in at most M frames" (TR-section-024) remains true with sprites included. The number of frames for a build of `U` units is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)`, plus one if the final commit needs its own `present`.
255	
256	**Order, inside one section.** Floor cells, wall-face cells, mounted cells, cap cells, then sprites in ascending `(kind_ordinal, idx)`. Sections build in ascending `section_id`. A chunk may end at any unit.
257	
258	**Staging and atomic commit.** A new or rebuilt section builds under the `Staging` holder (in the tree, `visible = false`, so `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` stays flat, V7) and `complete` flips only on the last unit. `body.projector` mounts a scene only when `complete`, in one pass, so no frame draws half a section. A rebuild of an already mounted section (a salvage that changes its template-visible state) builds a second set in `Staging`, keeps drawing the old set until the last chunk, then swaps (`swap_in`) in one apply; the same "old complete state keeps drawing" rule ADR-0009 § 2 states for the PROJECTOR. This ADR adds no exemption to the chunk budget for the Layout projector or `body.projector`: the single-chunk in-reach exemption in ADR-0009 § 1 belongs to Lighting's occluder builder only.
259	
260	**What is not chunked.** Anything a weld or cut needs in the first frame: reparenting and shifting nodes (§ 7), the socket-state sprites (bead, jambs, leaf, plate, scar: a handful of sprites, not tiles), root creation and freeing, the limits publish. These run in the stage-0 call that follows the notification, so the bead is drawn in the first rendered frame whose committed tick is at least the apply tick (TR-assembly-045); no bead sprite exists while `welds[]` has no row because the sprite set is built from `welds[]` and nothing else. The "last-projected cache" of the door leaf (ADR-0013 § 8) is read, not written, by the projector.
261	
262	**Readiness.**
263	
264	```gdscript
265	# src/presentation/projector/projector_readiness.gd (value-like; written by the two projectors, read by PipelineRoot)
266	class_name ProjectorReadiness extends RefCounted
267	var scene_epoch: int          # +1 on every complete commit or mount change
268	var pending_units: int        # work units still queued, all bodies in the ProjectionSet
269	var late_count: int           # ARRIVE_SCENE_LATE occurrences (DIAGNOSTIC only, never a SIM notification)
270	func is_ready() -> bool       # pending_units == 0 and every ProjectionSet section is complete and mounted
271	```
272	`PipelineRoot` reads `is_ready()` for the TRANSIT_HOLD latch (WM-14: "the Pipeline may cut to the avatar once its own projector latch also holds"; ADR-0008 is asked to add the read). When `DERELICT_LOADED` (or the arrival's `pod_settle`) is delivered while `is_ready()` is false, the projector increments `late_count`, logs `ARRIVE_SCENE_LATE`, and keeps building; the simulation is never delayed (E-19, TR-webmap-037). The arrival's worst-case build is the largest destination scene, home plus the welded derelict; its frame count is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)` with `U` counted from the real sections (a test builds it through `build_section`, not a hand sum), and `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` must cover it by the Web Map lint formula, whose numerator becomes the projector's work-unit count (tiles plus sprites) of the largest destination scene, not tiles alone (GDD Sync).
273	
274	**The projection set.** Scenes exist exactly for the sections the `ProjectionSet` names: the avatar's body (so the pod interior exists during a leg), the loaded set, and the arrival target while `ARRIVING` (it is still dormant then, WM-14). `body.projector` reads the avatar's body as `body_of_actor(actor_of_seat(local_seat))` from `BodyView` (the seat is injected at `setup()`), and the rest from a Web Map read (an assumption on ADR-0026: `web.view` publishes `projection_sections_into(out: PackedInt32Array) -> int`, ascending, including the arriving target). A section leaving the set is **freed** at the end of the next stage-0 pass, not hidden (a departed destination is rebuilt on return, which is the case the GDD sizes `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` for); retaining hidden scenes is a possible later knob, not built.
275	
276	### 7. Weld, cut, pod hop, restore: reparent and shift, rebuild as the reference
277	
278	**Decision.** On a weld or cut the projector **moves** the affected sections' existing nodes to their new body root and shifts their positions by the Layout-reported `frame_shift_px`; it **rebuilds no tile**. Rebuilding the whole destination scene on every weld was rejected (Alternative 4): it spends a chunked build, shows a frame boundary, makes two code paths for the same tree anyway, and gives no benefit because a moved section's geometry does not change.
279	
280	**The primitive.**
281	
282	```gdscript
283	# src/presentation/projector/scene_move.gd
284	class_name SceneMove extends RefCounted
285	## The one way to change a presentation node's parent. Local position is kept (reparent(p, false), probed; remove_child + add_child is equivalent). Never the one-argument reparent.
286	static func to(node: Node, new_parent: Node) -> void:
287		node.reparent(new_parent, false)
288	```
289	`Node.reparent(p)` with its default `keep_global_transform = true` rewrites the local position (V5), which would put a moved sprite at the wrong place, so it is banned outside this helper (`PJT-04`); TR-shipbody-032's "without using global-transform-preserving `Node.reparent`" is satisfied literally. After a move the node is the last child of its new parent; `SortedLayer` re-establishes order.
290	
291	**Weld (`AttachResult`, ADR-0013 § 7; `BODY_TRANSFER{weld}` and `BODY_DOCK_CONTACT`, ADR-0015).** In the stage-0 call that follows the notification, `body.projector`:
292	1. Reads the new `bodies[]` and `section_offset` of each section (Layout views). For every `SectionScene` whose `mounted_body_id` differs from `body_of(section_id)`, computes `delta = new_offset - mounted_off`, which equals the `frame_shift_px` of the weld for every moved section.
293	2. Moves the scene's four layer nodes to the matching group of the survivor root with `SceneMove.to`, and writes each layer's `position = new_offset` with `Placement.put`.
294	3. Moves the scene's `layout_sprites` to the survivor's `Mounted` or `PropsActors` `SortedLayer` according to class rank, shifting each by `delta` with `Placement.put(node, Vector2i(node.position) + delta)`, using `merge_from` so order is one pass.
295	4. Moves every **foreign attachment** whose `section_id` is a moved section the same way (§ 7.1), and every attached Presenter whose actor has a `BODY_TRANSFER` record to the destination `PropsActors` layer (the Presenter writes its own position later in stage 2, from `pos_curr` in the destination frame).
296	5. The socket-state sprites the weld changed (bead, jambs, leaf, plate, scar) were **already built by the Layout projector earlier in the same stage-0 pass** (it runs first, § 5), unchunked, from `welds[]` and the socket rows, into the still-mounted `SectionScene`s whose `static_version` moved; `body.projector` moves them with their scenes in steps 2 and 3 and builds nothing itself.
297	6. Frees the dissolved body's root (its groups are empty by now; a non-empty group is a defect, counted `PJT_ROOT_NOT_EMPTY`), recomputes and publishes `CameraLimits` (§ 9), updates every root's canvas offset (the canvas origin is now the survivor's frame), and bumps `scene_epoch`.
298	
299	The weld frame's cost is therefore proportional to nodes moved, not tiles built (V9 margin: the two reparent probes cost 0.08 to 0.3 ms on the dev machine). The node count after a weld equals the count before minus one root (`OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` flat, AC-BDY-92). The sort order of any sprite relative to a wall is unchanged because every key shifts by the same constant (the canvas origin change) and within-body relations are preserved; exact equal-key ties across the two bodies are the § 3.4 exception.
300	
301	**Cut (`DetachResult`, ADR-0013 § 7).** The mirror: a new `BodyRoot` for the new `body_id`, the moved components' scenes and foreign attachments moved and shifted by the re-base (`delta = offset_new - offset_old`), `BODY_TRANSFER{detach}` actors moved, limits recomputed for the avatar's body, and the new body's interior is hidden unless the avatar is on it (WM-19).
302	
303	**Pod hop.** Nothing is built or moved (a pod hop builds nothing, Web Map CF-LY); `BODY_TRANSFER{pod}` moves only the actor's Presenter node, and the camera cuts (ADR-0008 § 6.1). The canvas origin changes to the new avatar body, so every root's canvas offset is rewritten.
304	
305	**Restore, new game, `ALL`.** `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` frees every scene and root and rebuilds from the views through the same build path (staged, chunked, atomic). `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so nothing interpolates across the break. A scripted weld, cut and pod sequence through an incrementally updated projector and a fresh projector fed `ALL` must give equal `rebuild_signature()` values (ADR-0009 § 2 safety net, mandatory here: the projector is the first key-level incremental presenter whose two paths differ in kind).
306	
307	**7.1 The attach API (generalising `attach_presenter`).** Other presenters need a sanctioned way into the projector's tree so that reparent-on-weld is uniform:
308	
309	```gdscript
310	# src/presentation/projector/body_scenes.gd : the facade body.projector exposes (RefCounted, injected at setup())
311	class_name BodyScenes extends RefCounted
312	const OK: int = 0
313	const ERR_UNKNOWN_BODY: int = -1
314	const ERR_DUPLICATE_ID: int = -2
315	const ERR_BAND_DENIED: int = -3          # the band is projector-only (Floor, Faces, Caps) or the rank does not fit the band
316	const ERR_NO_SECTION: int = -4           # a non-actor attachment must name its section
317	## Attach a node a presenter built. The projector parents it, orders it, shifts it on weld and cut, and never frees it.
318	func attach(body_id: int, band: int, node: Node2D, class_rank: int, entity_id: int, section_id: int) -> int
319	## Remove the attachment; the node is left alive and parentless (the owner frees or re-attaches it).
320	func detach(node: Node2D) -> void
321	## The Avatar Presenter's registration (BDY-33 (f)): band PropsActors, class rank 3, entity_id = pack(BODY, actor_id), section_id 0.
322	func attach_presenter(actor_id: int, node: Node2D) -> int
323	```
324	Allowed bands for foreign nodes: `Marks` (Trail floor marks), `Mounted` (Trail wall trails, rank 1), `PropsActors` (Interaction and Suit items rank 2, Body actors and Horror rigs rank 3, off-floor web pieces rank 2), `Dust` (particles). `Floor`, `Faces` and `Caps` are projector-only. A non-actor attachment must name its `section_id` so the projector can move it with its section on a weld or cut; an actor attachment is moved by its `BODY_TRANSFER` record. The projector sets the group's z; the owner never writes `z_index`, which is what makes "no trail uses z 0 or +20" structural. When a body root is freed its foreign children have already been moved out; an attached node that is freed by its owner is dropped from the layer's arrays on the next `is_instance_valid` sweep (counted `PJT_ATTACH_DEAD`).
325	
326	### 8. Body roots: canvas offset and visibility
327	
328	**Canvas offset (the formula ADR-0015 hands to this ADR).** For every body root, with `avatar_body` the avatar's current body, `off_curr(b) = world(b) - world(avatar_body)` and `off_prev(b) = world_prev(b) - world_prev(avatar_body)` using the **current** avatar body for both terms (so a body switch never interpolates across two reference frames), and `position = Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, frame.alpha)`, written with `Placement.put` in stage 0 (`world`, `world_prev`, `vel` come from `BodyView`; `world` is exterior-only and bounded by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`, so every offset is within `2^23` and exact in `float32`). The avatar's body root is at (0, 0). A root whose offset did not change costs one skipped write.
329	
330	**Visibility (WM-19, defence in depth).** `BodyRoot.visible = InteriorDrawRule.visible(b, avatar_body, ...)`: true for the avatar's body and for a body docked or welded to it; false for a body drawn only as an exterior silhouette (those are not this tree). The rule is a pure function with injected inputs so it is unit-testable; its docked input is a Web Map read (an assumption on ADR-0026). Hiding a root hides its subtree and its lights' occluders are Lighting's concern.
331	
332	### 9. The camera-limit rectangle
333	
334	- **Value.** `CameraLimits` is a `RefCounted` with `valid`, `min_x`, `min_y`, `max_x`, `max_y` (integers, base px, half-open on the max side), `body_id` and `epoch`. `body.projector` is its only writer; `CameraSolver` (stage 1) reads it from `SolverInput` and is the only clamp. `Camera2D.limit_*` is never written (OQ-C closed, TR-pxl-017).
335	- **Frame.** The canvas is the avatar's body frame with the avatar's body at the origin (C2), so the rectangle is expressed in the avatar's body frame, which is also the canvas frame.
336	- **Rectangle.** The union, over `sections_of(avatar_body)`, of `[section_offset, section_offset + size_tiles x TILE_PX)` per axis (the template's `size_tiles`), grown on the **north** edge by `LIMITS_NORTH_OVERHANG = WALL_FACE_PX + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (a derived constant from two registered names; it lets the camera reach the top of the north wall's face and cap, which project up-screen above the footprint, PR-5). The three other edges are the hull envelope: "the void beyond a hull is honest black". No authored rect means `valid = false` and no clamp. The rectangle is **integer base px**; the solver's easing (`rect_eff`) and the inner-box-first order are ADR-0008's.
337	- **When.** Published in stage `PROJECT` on weld, cut, load, `ALL`, any `BODY`/`SEC` key of the avatar's body, and on a `BODY_TRANSFER` that changes the avatar's body; `epoch` increments on every change so the solver eases a changed rectangle and never pops it, except on a camera cut. Because stage 0 runs before stage 1, the solver consumes the new rectangle in the same frame as the `BODY_TRANSFER` rebase, in the new body's frame.
338	- **Clamp consequences owned elsewhere.** `CLAMPED` state, `world_to_hud` never offset while clamped, and the JOLT rule (at most `JOLT_PX`'s range, default 0, P1 events only, inside the viewport, never a container offset) are ADR-0008's; this ADR only guarantees that the projector never moves the camera and never offsets the canvas for a limit.
339	
340	### 10. The per-row z-band fallback (TR-pxl-009): specified, not built
341	
342	At MVP the sorted band is the single scope of § 2 and **the fallback is not built**. The reason is a probe-backed expectation, not a measurement: draw calls follow texture runs along the sorted order (V8), and with one sheet per layer the sorted layer is a handful of runs per row in view; the GDD's own 50 to 300 estimate is "NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike". The decision rule is the GDD's, made explicit:
343	
344	- **Trigger.** `D_ysort` (the world viewport's draw calls attributable to `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors`, measured by hiding those groups in a dev harness and reading `RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` per viewport) exceeds about 300 on a release export at the default field or at the largest ladder field.
