414	## Alternatives Considered
415	
416	### Alternative 1: Option B, one Y-sort node and no per-body roots
417	- **Description**: Every section's nodes keep one parent under a single Y-sort node; each section's position is driven from the body's pose plus `section_offset` every tick, so a weld changes an offset and never a parent (LY-31 option B, tried first by the spike).
418	- **Pros**: no reparent at all; the PR-5 "ONE Y-sort `Node2D`" is literal; a weld is a data change.
419	- **Cons**: its only advantage was keeping one sort scope, which nested `y_sort_enabled` nodes already give (V2). It also moves every section node and every sprite, not one root, whenever a body's canvas offset changes; it needs a per-node body-offset add in every Presenter (an actor then needs its body's offset on every `Placement.put`), which spreads body knowledge into every presenter; BDY-33's per-body root and AC-BDY-92 would be rewritten; and the freed-root, node-count and "the root disappears after a weld" checks lose their meaning.
420	- **Rejection Reason**: The premise (single scope needs a single parent) is false on 4.7.2 by probe, and B costs more writes and more coupling for no gain. Kept as a recorded comparison for SP-YSORT-1, not as a fallback.
421	
422	### Alternative 2: Band-first (class layers at world level, per-body translation sub-roots)
423	- **Description**: `World` holds the band groups; each band group holds one translation sub-root per body, so equal keys across bodies resolve by class rank everywhere.
424	- **Pros**: cross-body equal-key ties follow the contract exactly; PR-5's "ONE Y-sort node" stays closest to literal.
425	- **Cons**: the body offset is written once per band per body per frame (five to seven writes, mostly skipped by `Placement.put`); "one per-body root" in BDY-33 and TR-shipbody-032 becomes seven sub-roots that must be created, ordered and freed together; a weld must move sub-roots in every band; the visibility rule (WM-19) must toggle seven nodes.
426	- **Rejection Reason**: It buys exactness only in the docked-seam equal-key corner (§ 3.4) at the price of the registered "one root per body" shape. If SP-YSORT-1 observes a visible cross-body flip, this is the first remedy; the `BodyScenes` facade hides which shape is underneath, so the change would be local.
427	
428	### Alternative 3: One `TileMapLayer` per body (sections merged)
429	- **Description**: A single tile map per layer kind per body, cells in body-frame coordinates.
430	- **Pros**: fewer nodes; one `update_internals` per body.
431	- **Cons**: impossible on the 24 px grid: welded sections can be offset by half a 48 px tile (the registry's MVP offset is 14.5 tiles), so cells cannot align; a salvage or discard rebuilds the whole body; the maintained and `_worn` atlases would share a layer, and two atlas sources in one layer cost 440 draw calls against 1 (V8).
432	- **Rejection Reason**: Does not fit the geometry and costs draws. Per-section layers cost a few extra nodes (V9: 75 us to reparent one).
433	
434	### Alternative 4: Rebuild the body's scene on every weld and cut
435	- **Description**: Free the moved sections' nodes and rebuild them under the new root through the same chunked path as a restore.
436	- **Pros**: one code path; the scene is always a fresh function of the views.
437	- **Cons**: spends a chunked build on a change that moves geometry but does not alter it; the first frame after a weld may show a gap or a stale scene (the old set must keep drawing, so two sets exist); the bead's same-frame rule (TR-assembly-045) conflicts with chunking; allocations per weld rise; foreign attachments (trails, items) would be orphaned by the free and need re-attaching.
438	- **Rejection Reason**: Reparent and shift is cheaper and has no gap. The rebuild path is kept as the reference for restore and as the equivalence oracle (§ 7).
439	
440	### Alternative 5: `Node.reparent(parent)` with the default global-transform preservation
441	- **Description**: Let the engine rewrite the local position so the node stays visually still.
442	- **Pros**: no explicit shift arithmetic.
443	- **Cons**: the engine rewrites a float local position, bypassing `Placement.put`, and the shift is not the integer `frame_shift_px` Layout reports; TR-shipbody-032 forbids it by name; V5 shows the local position changes.
444	- **Rejection Reason**: Violates the single integer assignment point and the TR.
445	
446	### Alternative 6: Build the per-row z-band fallback at MVP
447	- **Description**: Wall faces, mounted items and sprites in world-anchored 24-row z bands from the start (PR-5 fallback as the default).
448	- **Pros**: removes any dependence on Y-sort batching behaviour.
449	- **Cons**: one `TileMapLayer` per band, sprites reparented at every band crossing, a union rectangle over all drawn bodies recomputed on dock, weld and detach, and the GDD itself says it is built only if it lowers both draw calls and CPU; V8 suggests the single sorted scope may already be cheap with one atlas per layer.
450	- **Rejection Reason**: Pays a certain complexity for a speculative gain; the go/no-go rule of § 10 stands.
451	
452	### Alternative 7: Tie-break by tree insertion order or by `x`
453	- **Description**: Let the engine's tie rule decide equal keys, or break ties by `x`.
454	- **Pros**: no ordering structure.
455	- **Cons**: tree order is not save-stable (a reload can reverse creation order); `x` makes an actor swap order with a prop as it walks along a row, which PR-5's acceptance forbids.
456	- **Rejection Reason**: Contradicts TR-pxl-006. The engine's tie rule is used, but only after `SortedLayer` has made the tree order equal the contract order.
457	
458	### Alternative 8: Non-sorting body roots
459	- **Description**: Only the groups are sorted; the body roots are plain translation nodes.
460	- **Pros**: matches "the cap layer is not a child of a Y-sort node" literally; each body is its own sort unit.
461	- **Cons**: a non-sorting intermediate sorts its subtree as a unit (V2): the two docked bodies would be ordered by root order alone, so a sprite of one body would draw over or under the other as a block, which is wrong at the seam.
462	- **Rejection Reason**: Breaks LY-31 exit criterion (1) across two bodies. The cap and floor lints are restated by band instead.
463	
464	### Alternative 9: The Layout projector parents directly under Body's root (no staging)
465	- **Description**: LY-31's text: Layout's PROJECTOR parents its section nodes under Body's root.
466	- **Pros**: no handoff object.
467	- **Cons**: ADR-0009 registers the layout projector before `body.projector`, so the root may not exist yet for a new body; reversing the order would alter ADR-0009 and the occluder builder's dependency; a half-built section would be visible under a live root.
468	- **Rejection Reason**: The staging handoff keeps ADR-0009's order and gives atomic commits.
469	
470	## Consequences
471	
472	### Positive
473	- The weld and cut frames do work proportional to nodes moved, with no tile build and no gap; the bead appears in the first frame.
474	- One merged sort scope, probed, keeps PR-5's draw order across docked bodies without a special case.
475	- `entity_id` is a pure function of persisted ids, so draw order is stable across save and reload; the namespace table closes Layout OQ-33 and the Pipeline's open registration.
476	- Foreign presenters (Trail, Avatar, Interaction, Horror) get one attach API, so reparenting on `BODY_TRANSFER` is uniform and no presenter writes a z number.
477	- Per-section layers localise rebuilds, free a departed destination cleanly and respect the 24 px grid.
478	- The camera-limits path is a plain integer value read in the same frame; ADR-0009 OQ-C and OQ-I are closed on the PROJECTOR side.
479	
480	### Negative
481	- Several GDD texts need rewording (§ GDD Sync): the wall-face `y_sort_origin == 24` lint, the "cap layer is not a child of the Y-sort node" lint, BDY-33 (d) and LY-31's default shape.
482	- Cross-body equal-key ties follow body order, not the comparator (§ 3.4).
483	- `SortedLayer` costs O(n) `move_child` calls on a merge and a binary search per insert; fine at the MVP's hundreds of nodes, a measured assumption on Deck.
484	- The projector depends on reads that other ADRs have not yet published (`ProjectionSet`, the docked set, the `JAMB` ordinal, the `area_max` invariant); each is listed.
485	- A y-sorted `TileMapLayer` costs 0.39 ms to update 453 cells on the dev machine (V9), against 13 us unsorted; acceptable margin on a desktop, unproven on Deck.
486	
487	## Risks
488	- **R1: Nested-sort and tie behaviour differs on a release export, on a 4.7 patch release, or under the project's pinned Vulkan Forward+ at scale.** The probes ran on the editor binary on one GPU. Mitigation: SP-YSORT-1 reruns V1 to V4 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release exports; the tree-walk test and `PJT-01` keep the shape; Alternative 2 is the local fallback for cross-body order.
489	- **R2: The tile key formula (V3) is relied on and undocumented in the pinned reference.** Mitigation: a boot self-test builds a two-cell fixture and reads back the order; a mismatch fails boot with `PJT_TILE_KEY_FORMULA`; the formula is recorded in the registry so a patch-release change is a one-line fix.
490	- **R3: Cross-body equal-key flip at the docked seam (§ 3.4).** Mitigation: ordered by `body_id`; recorded in SP-YSORT-1; remedy Alternative 2.
491	- **R4: `D_ysort` exceeds the budget with real art (96 px faces break texture runs per row).** Mitigation: the § 10 rule; per-field draw caps in ADR-0008 § 7; the fallback is specified.
492	- **R5: The weld frame or an arrival exceeds budget on Deck.** Mitigation: the unit is data (`BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`), the weld does no tile work, and a hitch is bounded by `WELD_FRAME_HITCH_MAX_MS`; a second ladder rung is to move the shift of far sprites into the next frame, which the equal-key rule tolerates only within a body.
493	- **R6: A presenter attaches a node and frees it behind the projector's back.** Mitigation: `is_instance_valid` sweep, `PJT_ATTACH_DEAD` counter, lint `PJT-06` on `queue_free` of an attached node.
494	- **R7: The `ProjectionSet` or docked inputs are not published as assumed (ADR-0026).** Mitigation: a default implementation uses the avatar's body only and logs; Open Questions OQ-A and OQ-B.
495	- **R8: Wall cell width and wall tile art are not specified.** The sort key does not depend on cell width, but the tile pitch on the x axis must hold 24 px footprints for side walls. Mitigation: routed to the asset spec; Open Question OQ-D.
496	- **R9: Orphan noise.** A staged subtree outside the tree counts as orphans (V7). Mitigation: `Staging` is in the tree and hidden.
497	- **R10: Float32 exactness of body offsets.** Offsets are bounded by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (ADR-0015); the release-export probe is ADR-0008's.

content.thinking:
Reparenting a TileMapLayer actually triggers a full rebuild of its cells, which contradicts the "no tile is rebuilt" assumption — this seems to be engine-side cost tied to the exit/enter tree cycle, proportional to cell count. I'm trying to reconcile this with the earlier ADR measurement, wondering if enter_tree just queues a deferred update rather than doing the rebuild immediately.

I also notice that a hidden staged layer shows zero runtime update calls — because TileMapLayer skips quadrant builds entirely when not visible in tree. That means the staged/chunked build does no real engine work while hidden, and the actual cost gets deferred to mount time, which undermines the whole chunk-budget strategy and the "weld cost is proportional to tile count, not atomic" claim. This feels like a blocking issue since it contradicts a core premise used to reject Alternative 4.

I'll go with blocking true since the ADR's measured claims were taken from a mismeasured scenario, and a quick extrapolation to the full 453-cell case still lands comfortably within budget at roughly 0.6ms. I'm also considering an alternative to the reparenting approach itself—keeping TileMapLayers under a stable per-section Node2D and reparenting that wrapper instead, to avoid disturbing the layer's own parent relationship.

That said, any reparent of an ancestor still triggers the same tree-exit/enter rebuild on the layer, so this doesn't actually dodge the cost. A better option might be the V2 approach of merging y-sort scope across the whole World, eliminating the need for per-body root reparenting in the first place—with per-body roots existing only for translation. I'll note this as an alternative but keep the primary plan as measure-and-accept the cost, and separately flag that the headless test shows a nonzero baseline orphan count that I can't easily verify is debug-only.

Since I can't fully verify tie-breaking order for y-sorted TileMapLayer cells in headless mode, I'm marking that unverified and considering a windowed rendering probe instead—setting up a SubViewport with overlapping tiles in different draw orders, then doing a pixel readback to see which tile renders on top before and after reparenting.

input.verdict: CONCERNS (1 blocking). No API in the ADR will fail to compile or does not exist on 4.7.2, and the 4.7 typed-return, packed-array-setter and const-object traps do not apply. But the headline claim "a weld rebuilds no tile" is false at engine level, and the V9 weld timing measured only the cheap half of the cost.

findings.text: Reparenting a TileMapLayer, or toggling an ancestor's visibility, makes the engine rebuild every cell. So 'no tile is rebuilt on a weld/cut' (Decision table, §7, Alt 4's rejection, Consequences, R5, V9) and the Staging pre-build idea (§5/§6, V7/R9) are wrong on 4.7.2. Probed headless 2026-10-29 with a TileMapLayer subclass that counts `_tile_data_runtime_update` calls on 100 y-sorted cells. (a) First build: 100 calls. (b) `update_internals()` with nothing changed: 0 calls, 39 us. (c) `reparent(b,false)` then `update_internals()`: 100 calls, 148 us. The same 100 calls occurred when the frame was awaited instead. (d) Unsorted layer with `rendering_quadrant_size` 16: 100 calls after reparent. (e) Parent `visible=false`: 0 calls on hide, 100 on show. (f) A layer built under a hidden parent: 0 calls while hidden (the engine builds nothing for a layer not visible in tree), then 100 when reparented into a visible parent. (g) Changing `position` caused 0 calls, so shifting a layer is free. The ADR's V9 '75 us reparent' times only the call. The EXIT_TREE/ENTER_TREE rebuild lands later, in the deferred internal update. Consequences: (1) a weld/cut costs about 0.9 us/cell per moved layer on the dev machine (453 sorted cells is about 0.4 ms, matching V9's own update_internals figure), proportional to tiles moved, unchunked and unmeasured for Deck. (2) The chunked build in Staging does only `set_cell` data work and the real quadrant/canvas-item build happens in one unchunked burst at mount, so BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME does not bound the arrival hitch, and §6's 'no frame draws half a section / chunk budget' reasoning is partly cosmetic. (3) Every WM-19 `BodyRoot.visible` flip rebuilds all layers under that root, and a root first shown after being hidden pays a full build.
findings.amendment: Reword the Decision table, §7, Alt 4, Consequences and R5 to say 'no tile is re-authored; the engine rebuilds the moved layers' canvas items once, deferred'. Replace V9's reparent figure with a probe of reparent plus the following frame or `update_internals()` on the real cell counts, windowed, release export, RM-DECK, and make that figure the weld budget term. Count the mount rebuild as U units against the arrival budget (or declare it unchunked and size ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS to it). State that Staging is a data stage only and does not pre-warm rendering. Add a zero-rebuild alternative to Alternatives Considered: give each section a permanent parent (a per-section y_sort_enabled Node2D under World, positioned at body canvas offset + section_offset) and never reparent, because V2 shows the merged scope does not need per-body parents and a position write was probed to cost 0 rebuilds. Also state whether BodyRoot.visible is used for WM-19 (rebuild on every flip) or the ProjectionSet frees and rebuilds, and measure that flip.

findings.text: The §3.3 order guarantee does not cover TileMapLayer children. `Mounted` is described as 'tile layers first, then sorted sprites', but SortedLayer's parallel arrays hold sprites only. `reparent(p,false)` appends the node as the last child (V5, confirmed by the ADR). After a weld the moved section's mounted/face layers therefore sit after the existing sprites, and `move_child(node, index)` indexes in SortedLayer's array are off by the number of layer children. At an equal key, a rank-1 tile (from layer order) and a rank-1 BEAD/PLATE/SCAR sprite (from entity_id) then tie by mount order, which is not save-stable. cross_adr.text: ADR-0008 §7.1 owns the draw-call table and the per-viewport `get_render_info` reading; ADR-0034 §10/§11 and V8 depend on that reading on release exports and on draw-call counts for hide/show harnesses. findings.text: Reparenting a TileMapLayer, or toggling an ancestor's visibility, makes the engine rebuild every cell. So 'no tile is rebuilt on a weld/cut' (Decision table, §7, Alt 4's rejection, Consequences, R5, V9) and the Staging pre-build idea (§5/§6, V7/R9) are wrong on 4.7.2. (d) Unsorted layer with `rendering_quadrant_size` 16: 100 calls after reparent. (e) Parent `visible=false`: 0 calls on hide, 100 on show. (f) A layer built under a hidden parent: 0 calls while hidden (the engine builds nothing for a layer not visible in tree), then 100 when reparented into a visible parent. findings.text: The section 3.3 order guarantee does not cover TileMapLayer children. `Mounted` is described as 'tile layers first, then sorted sprites', but SortedLayer's parallel arrays hold sprites only. `reparent(p,false)` appends the node as the last child (V5, confirmed by the ADR). After a weld the moved section's mounted/face layers therefore sit after the existing sprites, and `move_child(node, index)` indexes in SortedLayer's array are off by the number of layer children. At an equal key, a rank-1 tile (from layer order) and a rank-1 BEAD/PLATE/SCAR sprite (from entity_id) then tie by mount order, which is not save-stable. I probed that same-row cells inside one layer tie by x (higher x on top, identical whether cells are set 0,1 or 1,0, and after reparent), so intra-layer ties are deterministic. Ties across layers and across layer-versus-sprite are not.
findings.amendment: Add a LayerOrder step to SceneMove/body.projector: after every mount or move, `move_child` the group's TileMapLayers to the front, ordered by ascending section_id. Add `PJT` tree-walk and rebuild_signature checks for 'layers precede sprites in Mounted, layers by section_id'.

findings.text: Items checked and found sound on 4.7.2: `TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin`, `rendering_quadrant_size`, `update_internals()`, `TileData.y_sort_origin` and `Node.reparent(Node, bool)` all exist (ClassDB probe lists `y_sort_origin`, `x_draw_order_reversed`, `rendering_quadrant_size`). `EntityId` packing is valid: `127 << 56` stays positive in a signed int64 and `(1 << 56) - 1` is a valid const expression. `PackedByteArray`/`PackedInt64Array`/`Array[Node2D]` members are fine, with no packed-array setters involved. findings.amendment: None required. Optionally record in the ADR that the engine ties same-row cells of one y-sorted TileMapLayer by x, independent of set_cell order (probed in review, 4.7.2 Forward+).

data.verdict: CONCERNS (1 blocking). No API in the ADR will fail to compile or does not exist on 4.7.2, and the 4.7 typed-return, packed-array-setter and const-object traps do not apply. But the headline claim "a weld rebuilds no tile" is false at engine level, and the V9 weld timing measured only the cheap half of the cost.

findings.text: Reparenting a TileMapLayer, or toggling an ancestor's visibility, makes the engine rebuild every cell. So 'no tile is rebuilt on a weld/cut' (Decision table, section 7, Alt 4's rejection, Consequences, R5, V9) and the Staging pre-build idea (sections 5/6, V7/R9) are wrong on 4.7.2. Probed headless 2026-10-29 with a TileMapLayer subclass that counts `_tile_data_runtime_update` calls on 100 y-sorted cells. (a) First build: 100 calls. (b) `update_internals()` with nothing changed: 0 calls, 39 us. (c) `reparent(b,false)` then `update_internals()`: 100 calls, 148 us. The same 100 calls occurred when the frame was awaited instead. (d) Unsorted layer with `rendering_quadrant_size` 16: 100 calls after reparent. (e) Parent `visible=false`: 0 calls on hide, 100 on show. (f) A layer built under a hidden parent: 0 calls while hidden (the engine builds nothing for a layer not visible in tree), then 100 when reparented into a visible parent. (g) Changing `position` caused 0 calls, so shifting a layer is free. The ADR's V9 '75 us reparent' times only the call. The EXIT_TREE/ENTER_TREE rebuild lands later, in the deferred internal update. Consequences: (1) a weld/cut costs about 0.9 us/cell per moved layer on the dev machine (453 sorted cells is about 0.4 ms, matching V9's own update_internals figure), proportional to tiles moved, unchunked and unmeasured for Deck. (2) The chunked build in Staging does only `set_cell` data work and the real quadrant/canvas-item build happens in one unchunked burst at mount, so BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME does not bound the arrival hitch, and section 6's 'no frame draws half a section / chunk budget' reasoning is partly cosmetic. (3) Every WM-19 `BodyRoot.visible` flip rebuilds all layers under that root, and a root first shown after being hidden pays a full build.
